changes.before: Town of Lochbuie data-center moratorium ordinance approved July 21, 2026; the agenda identifies Ordinance 2026-720 while the town action summary says 2027-720, so the enacted number remains unresolved.
changes.after: Town of Lochbuie Ordinance 2026-720, adopted July 21, 2026; the signed ordinance and meeting minutes identify 2026-720, while the town action summary calls it 2027-720.

changes.before: Five-year pause on the Town's acceptance and review of applications for new or expanded data center facilities -- reported as the longest active data-center moratorium in Colorado.
changes.after: Five years from the ordinance's effective date, unless terminated earlier or extended by further ordinance. Section 8 sets effectiveness 30 days after final passage and publication by title. The pause has been reported as the longest active data-center moratorium in Colorado.

changes.before: Active as of 2026-09-23. Five-year moratorium on new/expanded data center facility applications, adopted 6-1 on July 21, 2026.
changes.after: Previously reported active as of 2026-09-23. Ordinance 2026-720 was adopted July 21, 2026 for five years from its effective date, subject to earlier termination or extension; subsequent current force has not been independently established in this review.

changes.before: Town Board passed a five-year moratorium on data center applications, the longest such pause reported in Colorado.
changes.after: Town Board adopted Ordinance 2026-720 by a 6-1 vote, imposing a five-year moratorium on covered data center applications from its effective date, subject to earlier termination or extension. The pause was reported as the longest such pause in Colorado.

changes.before: The newspaper reports a one-year moratorium through August 11, 2027. A town Resolution 15-26 copy instead states December 31, 2027, subject to earlier termination, extension or modification. The authenticated adopted version remains unresolved.
changes.after: Resolution 15-26 states a moratorium from August 11, 2026 through December 31, 2027, unless earlier terminated, extended, or modified. A newspaper reports a one-year term through August 11, 2027.

changes.before: The newspaper reports unanimous adoption of Resolution 15-26 and a one-year pause with a direction to draft regulations. A town resolution copy states a different end date; the operative adopted version remains unresolved.
changes.after: The town-posted signed Resolution 15-26 records adoption August 11, 2026, imposes a temporary moratorium through December 31, 2027 subject to earlier termination, extension, or modification, and provides for development of data-center regulations. The newspaper reports a unanimous vote and a conflicting one-year term through August 11, 2027.

changes.before: City Council voted 7-2 on September 15, 2026 to adopt the suspension, after amending the staff-proposed 9-month term to 12 months on a 5-4 vote (Councilor Laura Light-Kovacs' motion).
changes.after: City Council adopted Resolution R-48-2026 on September 15, 2026, after amending the suspension from nine to twelve months on a 5–4 vote and approving the amended resolution 7–2.

changes.before: City of Loveland Resolution (number not assigned in the draft text reviewed; adopted September 15, 2026)
changes.after: City of Loveland Resolution R-48-2026, adopted September 15, 2026 and effective upon adoption.

changes.before: 12-month suspension on the City's acceptance, processing, approval, permitting, rezoning, and site plan review of new land use applications for data centers with an electrical demand of 10 MW or more or that use industrial-scale cooling infrastructure; ends upon adoption of comprehensive Unified Development Code data-center regulations or 12 months from the effective date, whichever is first.
changes.after: 12-month suspension on the City's acceptance, processing, approval, permitting, rezoning, and site plan review of new land use applications for data centers with an electrical demand of 10 MW or more or that use industrial-scale cooling infrastructure; expires upon City Council approval, adoption and finalization of comprehensive data-center regulations within the Unified Development Code and/or Loveland Municipal Code or 12 months from the effective date, whichever occurs first, unless sooner terminated by City Council.

changes.before: A September 16, 2026 news report says council adopted a 12-month suspension on September 15 by 7–2, effective immediately and ending earlier if regulations are adopted. An October 13 report says staff told planning commissioners on October 12 that the moratorium began in October. The final effective date, end date and later legal force remain unverified.
changes.after: Resolution R-48-2026 was adopted and effective September 15, 2026. Its 12-month term yields a conditional end date of September 15, 2027, subject to earlier qualifying regulations or termination by City Council. An October 13 report said staff told planning commissioners on October 12 that the moratorium began in October; the signed resolution establishes the original effective date. Later action and current legal force remain unverified.
